hints: Split a mode like -rw-r----- into its parts: one character for the type, then three sets of three. Who does each set belong to, and which ones does the check actually read?
The likely mistake is thinking "everyone else" covers everybody but the owner. The group has its own set of three, between the owner's and everyone else's.
solution_explanation: After the first character, ls -l shows three sets of three: the owner, the group, and everyone else. A private file has no permissions in the last two sets, so the check reads the six characters after the owner's and makes sure they're all dashes.
